Proposed_Assumption_in_Phase_5_0: 300 mm w.e./yr annual surface snowmelt threshold triggers catastrophic ice-shelf collapse
Audited_Scientific_Reality: Trusel et al. (2015, Nature Geoscience) observed that Larsen A (1995) and Larsen B (2002) collapsed where melt reached 300–350 mm/yr.
Scientific_Validity_Verdict: VALID EMPIRICAL CORRELATION FOR HISTORICAL EMBAYMENTS, BUT INVALID AS UNIVERSAL PHYSICAL LAW
Recommended_Methodological_Resolution: Convert from deterministic threshold to probabilistic vulnerability curve conditioned on firn air depletion.

Proposed_Assumption_in_Phase_5_0: Meltwater immediately causes hydrofracture regardless of firn pore volume
Audited_Scientific_Reality: Kuipers Munneke et al. (2014) & van Wessem et al. (2016) proved collapse requires firn pore space exhaustion (FAC < 1.0 m). Without FAD, meltwater refreezes harmlessly.
Scientific_Validity_Verdict: SERIOUS PHYSICAL OMISSION IN PHASE 5.0 PROPOSAL
Recommended_Methodological_Resolution: Require decadal cumulative melt exceeding firn air content: integral(Melt - Refreezing) > FAC_0.

Evaluation_Criterion: Applicability to George VI Ice Shelf
Proposed_Assumption_in_Phase_5_0: Applied uniformly across all Peninsula basins including Basin Hp-I
Audited_Scientific_Reality: George VI routinely experiences >400 mm w.e./yr melt and extensive summer supraglacial lakes, yet has NOT collapsed for millennia.
Scientific_Validity_Verdict: COMPLETELY FAILS ON GEORGE VI (HIGH FALSE POSITIVE RISK)
Recommended_Methodological_Resolution: George VI is under compressive transverse stress (pinned by Alexander Island); hydrofracture requires net tensile stress (sigma_xx > 0).

Evaluation_Criterion: Applicability to Larsen C Ice Shelf
Proposed_Assumption_in_Phase_5_0: Deterministic collapse when melt exceeds 300 mm/yr
Audited_Scientific_Reality: Larsen C has thick firn (>15 m FAC in south). CMIP6 models project parts of Larsen C crossing 300 mm in 2050s, but firn depletion takes decades.
Recommended_Methodological_Resolution: Implement a two-stage model: (1) Firn saturation timescale (10–25 years); (2) Tensile hydrofracture trigger.
